subtopics.title: The Magnetic Field of a Current and the Right Hand Rule

questions.question: The magnetic field around a long straight current-carrying wire consists of:
options: Straight lines parallel to the wire
Concentric circles around the wire, closer together near the wire
Lines radiating outward from the wire
No field unless the wire is coiled

questions.question: In the Right Hand Rule for a straight wire, the thumb and fingers represent:
options: Thumb the field, fingers the current
Thumb the force, fingers the field
Thumb the conventional current, fingers the circular field direction

questions.question: Inside a current-carrying solenoid, the magnetic field is:
options: Strong, nearly uniform, and directed along the axis

questions.question: A scrapyard crane uses an electromagnet rather than a permanent magnet because:
options: The electromagnet can be switched off to release the load
Iron cannot be lifted by permanent magnets

subtopics.title: Magnetic Flux — Counting Field Through a Surface

questions.question: Magnetic flux is calculated as:
options: Φ = BA cosθ, with θ between the field and the normal to the surface
Φ = BA sinθ, with θ between the field and the surface

questions.question: The flux through a surface is a MAXIMUM when the magnetic field:
options: Lies in the plane of the surface
Is perpendicular to the surface, parallel to the normal

questions.question: A 0,05 m² coil sits in a 0,4 T field with the normal at 60° to the field. The flux is:

subtopics.title: Faraday's Law and the Direction of the Induced Current

questions.question: Faraday's law states that the induced emf is proportional to:
options: The strength of the magnet used
The rate of change of magnetic flux through the conductor
The steady flux through the coil

questions.question: A strong magnet rests motionless inside a coil. The induced current is:
options: Large, because the magnet is strong
Zero, because the flux is not changing

questions.question: A north pole is pushed toward the face of a solenoid. The induced current makes that face:
options: A north pole, to repel the approaching magnet
A south pole, to welcome the magnet
Alternate rapidly between north and south

questions.question: The induced current opposes the change that causes it. If it helped instead, the result would violate:
A 200-turn coil of area 0,03 m² has the field along its normal grow from 0,2 T to 0,8 T in 0,5 s. The emf magnitude is:
In ε = −NΔΦ/Δt, the quantity ΔΦ is:
options: The final flux through the whole coil multiplied by N
The strength of the magnetic field
The final flux minus the initial flux through one turn

questions.question: If that 7,2 V coil forms a closed circuit of total resistance 3,6 Ω, the induced current is:
Doubling the number of turns on a coil, with the same flux change in the same time:
Oersted's compass flinched when the current was switched on because:
options: The current produced a magnetic field around the wire
The battery attracted the needle electrostatically

questions.question: Coiling a wire into a solenoid is useful because:
options: It reduces the resistance to zero
The loops stack their fields into a strong magnet with a north and south end
It stops the field from escaping

subtopics.title: How Much Field Fits Through the Window?

questions.question: In the rain-and-bucket picture of flux, the rain, the bucket mouth and the tilt stand for:
options: Field strength, area and the angle factor

questions.question: A loop turned fully edge-on to a magnetic field catches:
A huge but perfectly steady flux through a coil generates:
options: No current at all — only changing flux induces current

questions.question: For eleven years after Oersted, magnets resting beside wires generated nothing because:
options: The missing ingredient was change — only changing flux induces current

questions.question: Pushing a magnet into a coil faster makes the induced current:
options: Bigger, because the flux changes at a greater rate

questions.question: The energy carried by an induced current ultimately comes from:
options: The work done pushing against the opposing induced effects

questions.question: A power station generator makes electricity by:
options: Spinning coils in magnetic fields so the flux through them changes continuously
Holding strong magnets perfectly still inside coils
